name: Markdown
instructions:
# Instructions

Refactor a Markdown parser.

The markdown exercise is a refactoring exercise.
There is code that parses a given string with [Markdown syntax][markdown] and returns the associated HTML for that string.
Even though this code is confusingly written and hard to follow, somehow it works and all the tests are passing!
Your challenge is to re-write this code to make it easier to read and maintain while still making sure that all the tests keep passing.

It would be helpful if you made notes of what you did in your refactoring in comments so reviewers can see that, but it isn't strictly necessary.
The most important thing is to make the code better!

[markdown]: https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/getting-started-with-writing-and-formatting-on-github/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax

#{parse_line(line)}

" end i += 1 end lines.join end private def parse_list(line : String, previous_line : Bool | String, next_line : Nil | String) : String result = "" if previous_line.is_a?(Bool) result += "

" end result end private def parse_heading(line : String) : String | Nil if line.starts_with?("#######") return "

example_solution:
class Markdown def initialize(@markdown : String); end def to_html result = "" lines = @markdown.split("\n") lines.each_with_index do |line, index| level = line.scan(/^#+/) if level.present? && level[0][0].size <= 6 level = level[0][0].size result += "#{parse_line(line[(level + 1)..-1])}" elsif line.starts_with?('*') result += "#{index == 0 || !lines[index - 1].starts_with?("*") ? "
    " : nil}
  • #{parse_line(line[2..-1])}
    • #{index == lines.size - 1 || !lines[index + 1].starts_with?("*") ? "
" : nil}" else result += "

#{parse_line(line)}

" end end result end private def parse_line(line : String) : String line.gsub(/__(.*?)__/) do |match| "#{match[2..-3]}" end.gsub(/_(.*?)_/) do |match| "#{match[1..-2]}" end end end
